items.headline: Uttarakhand SIR: 2,700+ names deleted in Gadarpur on objections filed by poll officers after the deadline
items.claim: Form 10 records published by Uttarakhand's Chief Electoral Officer show that Gadarpur's Electoral Registration Officer and ten Assistant Electoral Registration Officers filed 2,742 Form 7 objections on two dates, 763 on 18 September and 1,979 on 28 September, Newslaundry reported on 2 November. Claims and objections had closed on 13 August, and the final roll was published on 3 October. Rule 17 of the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960 requires an objection lodged after the period to be rejected. By the same records, objections against 4,785 names were filed by 13 August and against 2,825 after it, and the other 83 late objections were filed by individuals, 27 of them dated 14 August by a BJP leader. Of the 5,505 names deleted in Gadarpur after the draft, 2,496 followed objections by the assistant registration officers, 240 objections by the registration officer and 240 objections by private persons, and 2,529 were deleted with no objection recorded against them. Newslaundry met at least 15 deleted electors who said they learnt of it only after the final roll was published. Some said they had received a notice and others that they had received none, and all said officials told them to file Form 6 again. The registration officer, Amrita Sharma, told Newslaundry that officers had not known a Form 7 also had to be generated for electors marked absent, and that by the time this was noticed the hearings were over.
items.quote: Both dates fell more than a month after the claims and objections period ended on August 13, with the second batch just logged five days before the final electoral roll was published.
items.response: The registration officer said the late filings were a delay in generating the forms on the system, that hearings had already been held, and that these were Form 7 deletions on anomaly notices, which she distinguished from an officer's own proceedings under rule 21A. She said about 52,000 notices were issued in Gadarpur and about 45,000 electors heard and kept on the roll, that not a single name was deleted without a notice, and that the same ten assistant officers who filed the objections held the hearings. She said only forms submitted by 13 August were accepted and that the entries dated 14 August were uploads made late that night. On two electors who say they gave the documents asked for or had no notice, she said she would have to examine the records. She said more than 1,800 Form 6 applications had been received since the revision, over 900 of them from electors deleted for absence or other reasons. The report gives no reply from the Chief Electoral Officer or the Commission.
items.note: First reading, 10 November 2026. By Ashwine Kumar Singh and Basant Kumar in Newslaundry, published 2 November 2026 at 10:00 am IST (datePublished 2026-11-02T04:30:00Z), read in full from the page's JSON-LD articleBody with curl on 10 November 2026. 763 and 1,979 make 2,742, and with the 83 make 2,825. 2,496, 240, 240 and 2,529 make 5,505, which is the count of names deleted after the draft in Gadarpur on the site's Uttarakhand constituency table. items.headline: Thousands of votes marked for deletion in Andhra Pradesh without reasons on record
items.claim: The News Minute found that 40,006 electors were named for deletion in Form 7 applications in Andhra Pradesh between 29 September and 10 October, the last 12 days of claims and objections, and that 20,959 of them had an Electoral Registration Officer or an Assistant Electoral Registration Officer named as the objector in the Commission's consolidated Form 10 statements. Where an ordinary elector is the objector the statements give a reason, and where an officer is named they give none. In the 20 constituencies with the most names sought for deletion, officers were the objectors for 16,241 of 21,115. In Chandragiri the assistant officer is named 1,991 times and the officer 6 times among 2,452 names, in Palacole the officer 311 times and the assistant officer 1,701 times among 2,220, in Ongole the officer 1,277 times among 1,712, and in Narsapuram 1,369 times among 1,450. TNM could not read the statements from before 29 September, because each stays online for a week. The report sets out that rule 13(2) of the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960 lets only an elector on the roll object to an entry, and that section 22 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950 and rule 21A let the officer delete a name of his own motion after giving the elector a chance to be heard. Two registration officers and an assistant officer told TNM that the ERO-NET software shows no reason once the officer's login marks an elector ineligible, which generates the Form 7, and that it allows deletions to be uploaded in bulk.
items.quote: We noticed that when Form 7s are filed by normal citizens, the consolidated statement carries the reason for objection. But the reason for objection is not listed when an ERO or AERO is the objector.
items.response: TNM sent questions to Andhra Pradesh's Chief Electoral Officer, Vivek Yadav, and had no reply when it published. The Chief Electoral Officer answered on 28 October that the forms were generated through the software on the Commission's instructions for electors found ineligible after notices (form7-65). One registration officer told TNM that the officer is never in fact the objector, that the request comes from a family member or a booth level agent, and that his office holds documents to show it.

items.headline: Andhra CEO says no independent deletions. TNM’s questions about transparency remain
items.claim: Andhra Pradesh's Chief Electoral Officer answered TNM's report on Form 7s naming officers as objectors (form7-64) on 28 October, in a thread on the office's X account that says no registration officer or assistant registration officer deleted any name of his own motion. The thread says booth level officers found 44,89,512 electors not at their addresses between 15 June and 24 July 2026, and the draft roll of 31 July held 3,71,38,182 electors. Officers then sent notices to electors with no mapping or with data anomalies, and by 23 October another 1,73,701 electors had been found ineligible for the final roll. For each of them, the thread says, the officer passed a speaking order giving the reasons and uploaded it to ECINET, the booth level officer delivered the order to the elector with notice of an appeal to the District Collector, and a Form 7 was generated through ECINET in the officer's name as the Commission instructs, because a deletion takes effect in the system only after a Form 7 is generated. It calls the report's insinuations of procedural violations baseless and misleading and condemns them. The News Minute replied the same day that the statement does not say why officers appear as objectors in the published records or why no reason is shown in those cases.
items.quote: For deletion of all such electors, Form-7 have been auto-generated by the ERO / AERO through ECI-Net technically as per the ECI instructions.
items.response: The thread is the Chief Electoral Officer's own reply. TNM says its report did not allege that officers deleted names without due process, and that its question was why the public records give no reason for the deletions officers are named in. The thread does not say how many of the 20,959 electors in TNM's count are among the 1,73,701.

items.headline: As thousands were deleted from electoral rolls using auto-generated Form-7s, ECI gave no SOPs to State Electoral Officers
items.claim: Several State election officials told The Hindu that the Commission's software, ERONet, generated Form 7s automatically when officials deleted electors at the hearings of the revision, and that the forms carried the officers' digital signatures, the paper reported on 15 October. It named Delhi, Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand and West Bengal as states where officials had used this route to delete electors with unresolved logical discrepancies or with no mapping, and it said other reports had put the names deleted this way at more than 87,000 in Uttar Pradesh and more than 95,000 in Uttarakhand. The paper reported, from sources, that no written communication or standard operating procedure on these forms was shared with the election authorities in the states. It set out that the electoral rules make no provision for a registration officer or an assistant registration officer to file a Form 7, and that the Manual on Electoral Rolls, 2024 makes none for the registration officer to file one, though the officer, who decides objections, can delete a name found ineligible. The paper reports that the manual mentions auto-generated Form 7s only in the verification of Photo Similar Entries, where the forms ERONet generates are not filed by the registration officer and must be signed by the booth level officer after a field verification, or the system cannot accept or process them.
items.quote: According to several State electoral officials The Hindu spoke with, the ECI’s software, ERONet, automatically generated these Form 7s when officials deleted voters during the SIR hearings. The auto-generated forms came with the officers’ digital signatures.
items.response: The paper reported that the Commission had yet to answer an official query on the matter. Andhra Pradesh's Chief Electoral Officer said on 28 October that the forms in that state were generated through ECINET in the officers' names as the Commission instructs, for electors found ineligible after a notice and a speaking order (form7-65). Uttar Pradesh's Chief Electoral Officer's office called the account of such forms in that state misleading on 13 October, and said notices, hearings, scrutiny and recorded orders came before any action (up-02).
items.note: First reading, 11 November 2026. items.headline: Delhi SIR: Why BJP BLAs’ voter deletion applications in Mustafabad focused on three neighbourhoods
items.claim: The 796 Form 7 applications that name 20 booth level agents appointed by the BJP as objectors in Delhi's Mustafabad constituency are mostly concentrated in 25 of its 294 polling booths, in the neighbourhoods of Nehru Vihar, Dayalpur and Chandu Nagar, The Hindu reported on 10 November. The paper reports that all of them are against Muslim electors and that they are over 76% of the 1,044 deletion applications received in the constituency up to 4 November, from the published data. The applications give absence, a permanent shift or death as the reason, and the paper found at least 87 of the electors named living at their registered addresses. The paper reports, from an analysis of records and interviews with local BJP workers, that the 25 booths appeared to have been selected because they had a sizeable Muslim population and, by the workers' claims, few names left off the draft roll. BJP leaders who spoke to it on condition of anonymity said that after the draft of 31 August party workers compared the number of names placed on the list of absent, shifted, dead and duplicate electors in booths with a majority of Muslim electors and in booths with a majority of Hindu electors, prepared lists of Muslim electors, which the paper says it saw, and then concentrated on the 25 booths, where the agents began filing from the first week of October. The paper says it found copies of these booths' rolls, with the names of Muslim electors marked on them, with BJP workers in the area. It reports that the Commission's booth-wise figures do not bear out the workers' claim. By its count, names left off the draft averaged 274 a booth in Mustafabad and reached 538 at the most, and in most of the 25 booths they were close to the average. Parts 108 and 129, which it counts among the five booths with the fewest names left off the draft, carry 35 and 37 of the agents' applications. No application names a BJP agent in the other three, which BJP workers said were mostly Hindu. Nehru Vihar has the most applications, 496. The paper reports that none of the Form 7s received in Mustafabad came with the undertaking an agent must give.
items.quote: The Form 7 applications were all against Muslim electors, and the 25 booths, spread across three neighbourhoods, appeared to have been selected because they had a sizeable Muslim population with claims of few deletions when the draft electoral roll was published as part of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, an analysis of records and interviews with local BJP workers showed.
items.response: The Delhi BJP spokesperson, Praveen Shankar Kapoor, told the paper that the party's agents had not filed any Form 7s in Mustafabad, that the party had not directed any forms to be filed, and that booth level officers and the Commission would act on any objections under the rules. The BJP councillor for Nehru Vihar, Arun Bhati, said he was not authorised to speak about the applications, and said that some booths in Mustafabad had 300 to 500 votes deleted, which he said were coincidentally of Hindu voters, while others had fewer than 100, and that the two could not both be correct. The paper reports that officials maintain religious identity has no role in verification. The agent named in 57 applications told the paper he had filed them himself because the electors had shifted, and the councillor's brother, an agent named in 37, denied filing his. The report does not say how the paper established the religion of the electors or of each booth's population.

items.headline: Form 7 withdrawals, rejections follow Maharashtra scrutiny on false objections
items.claim: Amit Sanap, the electoral registration officer for Bhiwandi East, told the Hindustan Times that his office had received 540 Form 7 applications seeking deletions in the constituency and had rejected over 450 of them, because the electors the forms said were not living at their addresses were found living there. The paper reports that political parties' booth level agents filed 480 of the 540 and that some applicants could face criminal action for false information. Sanap said some applicants had withdrawn their applications and that action would begin once the formal orders were prepared. The paper reports that Form 7s filed by agents and private complainants have been withdrawn or rejected in large numbers on scrutiny in Mumbai and the constituencies around it, after Maharashtra's Chief Electoral Officer told registration officers to place the burden of proof on the objector, to summon objectors and verify their claims before acting, and to begin criminal action against false filings. A senior state election official told the paper that objectors are allowed to withdraw, and that withdrawals began once action started and the first FIR was registered in Dharavi three weeks earlier (form7-55). With claims and objections due to close on Friday, 13 November, the Commission had received over 23 lakh forms for additions, deletions and corrections in Maharashtra, more than 95,000 of them Form 7s, the paper reports.
items.quote: We received 540 applications seeking deletions through Form 7, of which over 450 have been rejected. We will initiate action once the formal orders are prepared. He said anyone with credible information about an incorrect registration has the right to file a Form 7 and that the authorised officer decides whether it is correct. The report does not say which parties' agents filed the 480 applications in Bhiwandi East.

items.headline: Delhi CEO's office to review SIR timeline as outreach to excluded voters awaits start
items.claim: Delhi's Chief Electoral Officer's office received 3,04,352 Form 6 applications for inclusion, 549 Form 6A applications, 30,954 Form 7 objections seeking deletion and 1,11,516 Form 8 applications for correction or shifting between the draft of 31 August and 11 November, according to the bulletin it issued on 12 November, Hindustan Times reported. The paper gives the totals with the applications received before the draft as 5,16,752 Form 6, 1,900 Form 6A, 82,425 Form 7 and 3,72,284 Form 8. Claims and objections close on 25 November, the applications are to be disposed of by 15 December and the final roll is due on 22 December. An official told the paper that the enumeration forms for electors left off the draft had not yet begun to be handed out, that this would begin the next week because the ECINet software was being updated, and that each booth level officer would have to reach about 300 such electors. PTI reported officials as saying that the Commission was changing the portal so that booth level officers could generate forms only for the electors left off, because at present forms are generated for all 1.45 crore electors in Delhi and the officers have to pick out those left off by hand. The official told Hindustan Times that the office would review whether the schedule needs a further extension, next week or closer to 25 November. The Tribune reported, from officials, that the Commission is considering an extension of about two weeks, which is yet to be approved and is to be discussed at the next meeting, and that nearly 15,000 booth level officers are expected to visit the registered addresses of the electors left off and hand them fresh forms.

items.headline: Over 23.6 lakh voter forms filled in SIR claims period in Maharashtra; no word on deadline extension from ECI
items.claim: Maharashtra received 23,60,021 applications for inclusion, deletion and correction on its electoral roll in its 36 districts from the draft of 31 August to 12 November, the day before claims and objections closed, The Times of India reported on 14 November from the district figures released by the state election office. The paper reports that 15.18 lakh of them were Form 6 applications for inclusion, 1.25 lakh were Form 7 applications seeking deletion and 7,15,729 were Form 8 applications for correction. Hindustan Times, reporting the same figures on 14 November, gives 1,25,693 Form 7 applications. Mumbai Suburban received the most applications, 1,91,308, followed by Pune with 1,65,446 and Thane with 1,64,834, and Sindhudurg received the fewest, 16,098. Election officials told The Times of India that the count includes only the applications filed online, because the forms submitted on paper had not yet been digitised, and that it leaves out the applications received on 13 November, the last day, so the final count will be higher. The paper reports that the applications are to be disposed of by 25 November and that the final roll is to be published on 30 November.
items.quote: Of the 23,60,021 forms received across 36 districts till Nov 12, as many as 15.18 lakh were Form 6 applications for inclusion of names in the electoral roll.
items.response: The Times of India reports that the Commission had not announced any further extension of the period for claims and objections when the paper went to press, although opposition parties and activists had asked for one. items.headline: EC relief to 99.4% electors served notices during SIR in Maharashtra
items.claim: Of the 12.24 million electors on Maharashtra's draft roll who were served notices, 6.25 million for discrepancies in their names, ages, addresses and other details and 5.98 million because they could not be mapped to the 2002 roll, 99.41 per cent have cleared and 72,601 have not, because they have yet to submit documents or their documents are still being checked, Hindustan Times reported on 14 November. The Times of India reported the same day, from the latest data released by election officials, that 99.4 per cent of the 1.2 crore electors served notices had cleared scrutiny and would stay on the roll. It gives 99.6 per cent of the 62.5 lakh served notices for discrepancies and 99.2 per cent of the 59.7 lakh served notices as unmapped. An official of the Chief Electoral Officer's office told Hindustan Times that documents can be submitted and verified until 23 November and that more of these electors are expected to be cleared. Both papers report that Nandurbar has the highest share cleared, 99.99 per cent, and Nanded the lowest, 96.18 per cent, followed by Jalna at 96.83 per cent. Both give Mumbai City at 99.61 per cent, Mumbai Suburban at 99.73 per cent and Thane at 99.88 per cent, and The Times of India gives Pune at 98.91 per cent. Hindustan Times reports that the share rose after the Commission relaxed its guidelines. By its account, personal hearings with booth level officers were dropped, documents could be sent on WhatsApp and PAN and Aadhaar details were accepted. Registration officers told the paper that after the protests across the country booth level officers were told to be lenient and could decide for themselves whether to ask an elector for more details.
items.quote: The last day for submission of documents and their verification is November 23. We expect a few more voters to be added back to the rolls from this lot,
items.response: None of the officials is named in either report. A senior official of the Chief Electoral Officer's office told The Times of India that the figure showed that in 99.4 per cent of cases the documents and information supplied by the electors served notices were found satisfactory. Neither report gives a response from a political party, and neither says what will happen to the 72,601 electors whose cases are still open on 23 November.
